reason: The cited evidence shows that single-phase lightweight HEAs can be formed (E2) and that Al/Ti additions often produce multiphase structures (E1), but none of the passages provide direct support for the claimed synergistic mechanism of lattice distortion plus controlled surface segregation improving corrosion and oxidation resistance, nor do they compare single-phase vs. multiphase alloys on all three properties.
premises: Single-phase solid solution in lightweight HEAs can be achieved by processing and alloying
Severe lattice distortion in single-phase HEAs impedes dislocation motion and increases strength
Controlled surface segregation of Al and Cr promotes protective oxide films
Multiphase microstructures with intermetallics are detrimental to strength and corrosion/oxidation resistance
Single-phase lightweight HEAs can simultaneously deliver high specific strength, corrosion resistance, and oxidation resistance
